summary: American cartoonist Hank Ketcham scabbed during the 1941 Disney strike, built Dennis the Menace on his son, then neglected him, hid his mother's death and sent him away, and drew a racist caricature in 1970.
keywords: The Merchant of Dennis the Menace

evidence.note: long segment on the 1941 Disney animators' strike and union demands
Ketcham leaves the picket line and crosses it to keep working
son Dennis born 1946, namesake and model for the strip
October 1950 incident that inspired the strip; launch in March 1951
twelve-year-old Dennis sent to boarding school after the separation
father withholds news of the mother's death until after the burial
move to Switzerland with new wife; son placed in a Swiss school, then sent back
1970 introduction of a caricatured Black character and the backlash
Dennis joins the Marines, serves in Vietnam, returns with PTSD
Ketcham dies in 2001; son does not attend the funeral

notes: Primary theme child-abuse reflects emotional neglect and abandonment by a parent, not physical or sexual abuse; entertainment-celebrity was the alternative. Dennis Ketcham's death year is not stated in the packet (the host does not know if he is alive), so lifespan end is null. main_span starts at the strip's conception in 1950; the 1941 strike is inside covered_span.
